channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Officials weigh Iran’s role in up to 50 tanker cyberattacks, widening the Coast Guard’s confirmed boardings of US-bound ships
item.description: US officials told the Wall Street Journal, in a report carried on 23–24 November, that Iran is the main suspect in as many as 50 cyberattacks on tankers carrying oil, gas and chemicals; Russia is also being examined, and an administration official says there is no evidence of Iranian involvement. The report widens a case first made public in September, when the Coast Guard and FBI confirmed boarding two foreign-flagged, US-bound tankers in August after signs their networks had been compromised. Cyber teams have since assisted at least four US-bound vessels, including the VL Prosperity, which received a ransom note and a bomb threat. Bloomberg reports that hackers reached one supertanker’s propulsion system, which is not confirmed, and the suggested Fortinet entry route is unsettled. For OT defenders, vessel and terminal networks, and the edge devices that reach them, are now live targets. - Reuters, via US News (23 Nov 2026, WSJ report); SecurityWeek (17 Sep 2026, original boardings); Fox News (23 Nov 2026, Coast Guard/FBI boarding statement); Maritime Executive (24 Nov 2026, incl. FT port reporting); TechCrunch (24 Nov 2026); Gulf News (24 Nov 2026); Security Boulevard (24 Nov 2026); TechTimes (25 Nov 2026, Bloomberg propulsion report and FortiBleed context) - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026, first confirmed Sep 2026; WSJ report widening the case 23 Nov 2026; follow-up coverage to 25 Nov 2026; no formal US attribution

item.title: [Critical] CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
item.category: Incident — CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT joint warning (5 Nov 2026) and a second wave of refrigeration attacks across about 11 European countries (1–4 Nov); Belgium says its evidence points to Iran (12 Nov), no formal attribution
item.description: Hackers are tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers in European supermarkets; on 5 November CISA and the FBI, with HHS, USDA and DOT, warned the threat is ongoing and reaches healthcare, chemical, transport and cold-storage operations. Hundreds of French stores were hit in October; a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost, and three French blood-service sites had settings changed with no blood lost. Sweden’s NCSC says victims at Coop and ICA stores mainly ran older systems from one manufacturer with weak passwords. Belgium’s interior minister said on 12 November that evidence points to Iran, short of formal attribution. Sekoia says the second wave used a non-public, unauthenticated flaw that renames the controller’s admin account. If a controller is reachable from the internet, treat it as at risk today. - TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); SentinelOne Labs (3 Nov 2026, updated 4 Nov); Cybersecurity Dive (3 Nov 2026, updated with 4 Nov developments); Unit 42 (6 Nov 2026, exposure counts); Censys (6 Nov 2026, exposure analysis); BleepingComputer (5 Nov 2026); Nextgov (29 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera (4 Nov 2026); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012; The Cyber Express (6 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory summary); Industrial Cyber (6 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (6 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (6 Nov 2026, hardening guidance); The Hacker News (9 Nov 2026, exposure trend); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish government and NCSC warning); Arab News/AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement); Sekoia TDR (10 Nov 2026, second-wave technique) - Attacks overnight 1–2 Nov 2026; Germany, Romania and UK confirmed 4 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov 2026; French attribution of the October attack 9 Nov 2026; Swedish government warning 10 Nov 2026; Belgian minister points to Iran 12 Nov 2026 — investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct; Siemens adds metering gateways 16 Nov
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials. Siemens (Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways), Schneider (a Foxboro DCS server) and ABB (Netcontrol RTUs, ASPECT gateways) now list affected products, several unfixed. None is reported exploited and no OT operator is named: treat it as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026, WTV676/WTV776 added; V1.2 29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A Chilean solar-and-battery plant is still off the grid nearly three months after a cyberattack, and lawmakers want answers
item.category: Incident — cyberattack forced Chile’s 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant and its battery system off the grid (attack 26 Aug 2026, forced disconnection 27 Aug); still offline per the 14 Nov 2026 grid-coordinator report; congressional information requests filed 11 Nov 2026; no attribution
item.description: The 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant in Chile’s Tarapacá region, with a 98 MW / 312 MWh battery system in commissioning, has been off the national grid since the National Electric Coordinator triggered its disconnection protocol on 27 August after a reported cyberattack. Its 14 November report still lists both assets at zero availability. On 11 November a member of Congress asked whether the national cybersecurity agency was notified as the law requires and which control systems were hit; no answer by 16 November. The owner, entry route and affected systems are undisclosed. The lesson: a plant pulled off the grid for safety can stay dark for months if it cannot be restored with confidence (editorial assessment). - ESS News / pv magazine (17 Nov 2026, citing Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional records); T13 (16 Nov 2026, in Spanish); pv magazine Latin America (16 Nov 2026, congressional requests, in Spanish) - Ongoing — still offline per 14 Nov 2026 coordinator report; congressional requests 11 Nov 2026; reported 16–17 Nov 2026; attack 26 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Illinois investigates an apparent cyberattack attempt on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River
item.category: Incident — Attempted cyberattack on the state-run Algonquin Dam, Fox River, Illinois (16 Nov 2026; disclosed by IDNR 20 Nov 2026); dam kept secure and operating; CISA and state agencies investigating; no attribution
item.description: The Illinois Department of Natural Resources said on 20 November that it detected an apparent attempted cyberattack on the Algonquin Dam, about 45 miles northwest of Chicago, on 16 November. Staff blocked the unauthorised access at once, and the dam stayed secure and fully operational. IDNR has not said which system was targeted or whether gate controls were reachable. Illinois State Police, state agencies and CISA are investigating; no link to other attacks and no group has been named. For dam and flood-control owners, it is a prompt to check who can reach gate and spillway controls remotely (editorial assessment). - CBS Chicago (20 Nov 2026); ABC7 Chicago (20–21 Nov 2026); BNO News (21 Nov 2026); all citing the Illinois Department of Natural Resources - Attempt 16 Nov 2026; disclosed 20 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [Critical] Peninsula Energy shuts its Wyoming uranium plant and wellfield after a cyberattack reaches their control systems
item.category: Incident — Updated 25 Nov 2026: Peninsula Energy confirms the attack hit plant and wellfield operating and control systems at its Lance uranium project, Wyoming (found 20 Nov 2026); site shut down; shares suspended to 30 Nov; no attacker named
item.description: Peninsula Energy said on 25 November that the incident its US subsidiary Strata Energy found on the morning of 20 November hit the plant and wellfield operating and control systems at its Lance in-situ uranium project in Crook County, Wyoming. Lance has been shut down and the affected systems isolated; corporate and administrative systems in the US and Australia, including payroll and finance, are unaffected. US authorities were notified and outside forensic advisers engaged. The company cannot yet say whether 2027 production guidance is at risk, and its shares are suspended until 30 November or a restart announcement. The entry route and attacker are undisclosed and no group has claimed it. A control-system hit that forces a full shutdown is the case a rehearsed safe-state plan exists for (editorial assessment). - Peninsula Energy ASX update (25 Nov 2026), via Discovery Alert; Peninsula ASX trading-halt request via Listcorp (23 Nov 2026); Cowboy State Daily (23 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Nov 2026) - Incident found 20 Nov 2026; halt 23 Nov 2026; control-system impact and shutdown confirmed 25 Nov 2026; suspension to 30 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Switzerland confirms its first AI-agent cyberattacks: four of five succeeded, and power, water and telecom operators were among the targets
item.category: Incident — AI-agent-driven intrusions at Swiss companies and critical-infrastructure operators (BACS, 26 Nov 2026); whether IT or OT systems were hit is not disclosed
item.description: Switzerland’s Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) said on 26 November that five attacks in recent days used AI agents, frameworks that find weaknesses, pick tools and plan their next steps largely on their own. Four of the five compromised systems. Three targets were critical-infrastructure operators, which public broadcaster SRF identified as electricity, water and telecommunications providers. BACS named no victims or attacker and has not said whether any control systems were reached. The reported entry points were ordinary: default or easily guessed passwords and known flaws in internet-facing systems. The UK NCSC described the same pattern on 24 November. AI is not inventing new attacks; it is hitting old weaknesses much faster (editorial assessment). - Reuters, via Global Banking & Finance Review (26 Nov 2026, BACS statement); SRF (26 Nov 2026, sector detail, via Reuters); EM360Tech (26 Nov 2026); UK NCSC blog (24 Nov 2026, agentic-attack guidance) - BACS statement reported 26 Nov 2026; attacks in the preceding days; victims and attribution not released

item.title: [High] Ransomware halts smart-meter production and shipments at Japan’s Osaki Electric
item.category: Incident — Updated 25 Nov 2026: ransomware at Japanese smart-meter maker Osaki Electric (confirmed 17 Nov 2026) halted production and shipments; data exfiltration confirmed and a staged restart from 27 Nov planned; no group named
item.description: Osaki Electric, a Japanese smart-meter maker, said ransomware encrypted data on its servers on 17 November, and it suspended production and shipments at its Saitama centre and at group companies Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platech. The company believes the intruder got in on 15 November through a VPN device by guessing the password of an account without multi-factor authentication. In a 25 November update it confirmed data was sent from internal systems to an outside destination, said production equipment and meters already in customer use are unaffected, and set a tentative plan: staged production from 27 November, shipments of existing orders from 1 December and new orders from 7 December. No group has claimed it. For utilities the risk is supply-chain: delayed meter rollouts and how suppliers protect the systems that build and sign devices (editorial assessment). - Osaki Electric announcements, via TipRanks (17 Nov 2026; updated 18 and 20 Nov 2026, entry route and data leak); Osaki 25 Nov 2026 update, via Viakoo/Security Boulevard daily OT briefing (25 Nov 2026); Industrial Cyber (24 Nov 2026, OT-ISAC supplier-continuity warning); NHK (18 Nov 2026, in Japanese); Kyodo, via Yahoo! Japan News and Tokyo Shimbun (18 Nov 2026, in Japanese) - Intrusion estimated 15 Nov 2026; attack confirmed 17 Nov 2026; entry route disclosed 20 Nov 2026; exfiltration confirmed and staged restart planned from 27 Nov 2026 (update 25 Nov 2026)

item.title: [High] Cyberattack on Brazil’s Santos port authority forces manual workarounds at Latin America’s busiest port
item.category: Incident — Cyberattack on the Santos Port Authority (APS), Brazil; systems down from 6 Nov 2026, attack confirmed 10 Nov; port security raised to level 2 of 3 (8 Nov); core systems in final tests 16 Nov 2026; about 70% of backups recovered; Federal Police inquiry opened 10 Nov; no attribution
item.description: The Port of Santos authority, which runs Brazil’s largest port, lost its IT systems on 6 November and on 10 November confirmed a cyberattack. Access-control systems and digital tools for coordinating port operations went down, delaying vessel, truck and train procedures and forcing some checks, such as matching ship dimensions to berths, to be done by hand. The port’s protection level was raised to 2 of 3 on 8 November. By 16 November main internal systems were in final tests and about 70% of affected file backups were recovered; ship movements and landside access continued throughout. Brazil’s Federal Police are investigating; the attacker, entry route and any data theft are undisclosed. For port operators, access control and berth planning need a tested manual fallback (editorial assessment). - The Rio Times (16 Nov 2026, status update citing the Santos Port Authority); DatamarNews (10 Nov 2026, updated 11 Nov, citing A Tribuna); CyberDelegate (17 Nov 2026, citing Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil and Agência Brasil); Interlira Reports (17 Nov 2026) - Outage from 6 Nov 2026; security level raised 8 Nov 2026; attack confirmed 10 Nov 2026; core systems in final tests and ~70% of backups recovered 16–17 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [Medium] SAP investigates a breach that German media say reached its GitHub source code, raising supply-chain questions for plants that run on SAP
item.category: Incident — SAP confirms it is investigating a cybersecurity incident (reported 27 Nov 2026); German media report stolen GitHub tokens and altered source code; no customer impact confirmed
item.description: SAP says it is investigating a cybersecurity incident after detecting suspicious activity and that, so far, it has found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data. Der Spiegel, citing insiders, reports that attackers stole employees’ GitHub authentication tokens and used them to copy and alter source code; Handelsblatt says SAP replaced signing keys, restricted GitHub access and paused automated development. It is not clear whether proprietary code was touched, and no report says altered code reached customers. A late-October leak-site claim by The Gentlemen ransomware group does not appear to be connected. Many manufacturers and utilities link SAP to plant maintenance, production planning and MES, so the integrity of SAP updates matters on the plant side too (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (27 Nov 2026, citing SAP’s statement and reporting by Der Spiegel, Handelsblatt and DPA) - Incident and reports 26–27 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [Medium] Booba ransomware moves from a US water treatment plant’s network into the local government that runs it
item.category: Incident — Booba ransomware staged on an unnamed East Coast water treatment plant’s network and spread to the overseeing local government (November 2026; reported by ThreatDown 24 Nov 2026); no OT impact reported; no attribution
item.description: Managed-detection firm ThreatDown said on 24 November that Booba ransomware, a group that surfaced only this summer, was staged on the network of an unnamed East Coast water treatment plant in November and then spread into the network of the local government that oversees it. The plant side was run by a separate provider without ThreatDown coverage, and encryption launched from an unprotected machine there. ThreatDown says it isolated 48 government machines, three already encrypted, and the plant’s computers were taken offline for on-site remediation. No source says SCADA, PLCs or treatment were affected, and the utility is not named. ThreatDown says Booba accounts for 44% of the ransomware cases it handled in the past 90 days. A network shared by a small utility and its town lets one weak segment expose both (editorial assessment). - ThreatDown (Malwarebytes) blog (24 Nov 2026), reposted by Malware News (25 Nov 2026); Industrial Cyber (Nov 2026); Finexus (27 Nov 2026, aggregator) - Attack in November 2026; reported 24 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] An IT intrusion stops production at all three Kinnarps factories in Sweden
item.category: Incident — IT attack on Swedish office-furniture maker Kinnarps (detected 7 Nov 2026) stopped production at all three of its factories (9–10 Nov); gradual restart from 13 Nov; attacker unknown, no ransom demand
item.description: Kinnarps, one of Europe’s largest office-furniture makers, detected an intrusion on the evening of 7 November and shut down its systems and servers to contain it. By 9–10 November production had stopped at all three of its Swedish factories, in Kinnarp, Jönköping and Skillingaryd, which employ about 920 people. The company reported the attack to police, said it had received no ransom demand and said it had found the entry route, without saying what it was; the attacker is unknown. Production restarted gradually from 13 November. It is not public whether data was taken or whether plant systems were reached directly. A defensive IT shutdown can stop a factory as surely as an attack on its controllers (editorial assessment). - Placera/TT (10 Nov 2026, in Swedish); Dagens PS (Nov 2026, in Swedish); SVT Nyheter Väst (company statement, in Swedish); Falköpings Tidning (13 Nov 2026, gradual restart, in Swedish); CADChain BORIS blog summary (16 Nov 2026) - Intrusion detected 7 Nov 2026; production stopped 9–10 Nov 2026; gradual restart from 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] A new water supply-chain index finds almost twice the vulnerabilities public records show, including 20 exploited flaws missing from CISA’s KEV list
item.category: Research — Securin “Water Supply Chain Watch” index of vulnerabilities in technology vendors supplying US water systems (reported 25 Nov 2026)
item.description: Securin’s Water Supply Chain Watch, reported by The Register on 25 November, compared data on 236 technology vendors serving US drinking-water, wastewater and industrial-water systems against CISA, EPA, FBI and WaterISAC records. It found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identify, including 20 exploited flaws that are not in CISA’s KEV catalog. Five vendors account for about half of 376 water-tagged advisories: Rockwell Automation, Advantech, Schneider Electric, Siemens and ABB. Securin also counted 791 internet-exposed Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers as of 17 November, the model family hit in this summer’s water-utility attacks. Utilities that patch only from the KEV list will miss exploited flaws in their own gear (editorial assessment). - The Register (25 Nov 2026, citing Securin); Securin Water Supply Chain Watch (Nov 2026; CISA advisory data through 20 Nov, KEV through 23 Nov) - Reported 25 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] GreyNoise says an AI-assisted crew breached Check Point firewall-management servers at 22 organizations, including energy, transport and manufacturing firms
item.category: Research — GreyNoise “GT13” campaign against Check Point Security Management servers (activity 17 Oct–2 Nov 2026, reported 24 Nov 2026); at least 22 organizations breached; unattributed
item.description: GreyNoise reported on 24 November a campaign it tracks as GT13 that compromised Check Point Security Management servers at at least 22 organizations in several countries between 17 October and 2 November; it lost visibility after that and believes attempts continue. Victims include energy, transportation, mining, engineering and manufacturing firms. The attackers used a Rejetto HFS file server as a relay, then CVE-2026-16232 in SmartConsole to run scripts on management servers, copying firewall databases and internal certificate authorities and unloading security policies. GreyNoise believes AI tools did much of the work with human operators involved, and cannot name the group or country; Check Point says no new vulnerability or technique is involved. A firewall manager holds the rulebook for the IT/OT boundary, so a stolen policy database is a map of the plant perimeter (editorial assessment). - GreyNoise research, via Cybersecurity Dive (24 Nov 2026) and Security Affairs (25 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Nov 2026) - Activity 17 Oct–2 Nov 2026; reported 24 Nov 2026; attempts believed ongoing

item.title: [High] A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) exploited as a zero-day for more than two months by a suspected China-linked group, per Mandiant; Broadcom fix released 19 Nov 2026; no public fix for vCenter 7.0
item.description: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported the bug, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221, also called Warp Panda) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the incidents Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, moved to Linux appliances, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, created an SSO admin account, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Many plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Broadcom, Google Threat Intelligence/Mandiant and Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal); CISA KEV alert (20 Nov 2026); The Hacker News (20–21 Nov 2026) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; patched 19 Nov 2026; exploited from at least early Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] CISA confirms exploitation of three Danfoss refrigeration-manager flaws, while the two newest critical CVEs have no fix until firmware 5.5.x
item.category: Active exploitation — CISA adds three Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws (CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, CVE-2025-41450) to KEV (25 Nov 2026); Danfoss DSA-2026-12-01/-02 (20 Nov): CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS v4 9.3) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS v4 9.9) still have no fix
item.description: On 25 November CISA added three flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A system managers, the store-level controllers that run supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: path traversal CVE-2023-25914, input-validation flaw CVE-2023-25915 and authentication flaw CVE-2025-41450. It is the first official confirmation that Danfoss weaknesses themselves are being exploited in the wild, although CISA named no actor and did not link them to the European attacks (see Incidents & Attacks). The listing follows Danfoss’s 20 November advisories for CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS v4 9.3, AK-SM 8xxA up to firmware 5.4.0), fixed only in the coming 5.5.x release, and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS v4 9.9, documented default credentials on legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 units). US federal agencies must fix two of the KEV flaws by 28 November and CVE-2025-41450 by 9 December. Keeping these units off the internet remains the real control. - CISA KEV alert (25 Nov 2026), via Cyber Security News (26 Nov 2026) and Shattered.io (26 Nov 2026); CISA ICSA-26-328-03 (24 Nov 2026, CVE-2026-129713 at CVSS v3 9.8); Danfoss DSA-2026-12-01 and DSA-2026-12-02 (20 Nov 2026); Infosecurity Magazine (Nov 2026); Midnight Blue (Nov 2026); The Hacker News (16 Nov 2026, CCB, BSI and Irish NCSC warnings) - Added to CISA KEV 25 Nov 2026; CISA republication 24 Nov 2026; Danfoss advisories and CVEs 20 Nov 2026; CCB and BSI warnings 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.category: Advisory — OpenJDK “Java4Shell” memory-corruption flaw CVE-2026-114938 (disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026); exploitation attempts seen 18–19 Nov 2026; Siemens SSA-272816 lists three Industrial Edge Management products
item.description: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched. - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Calif, GreyNoise, WatchTowr, Cloudflare, Previdian, Siemens SSA-272816, Cisco and Atlassian); The Record (18 Nov 2026, CISA alert) - Disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026; exploitation attempts 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Comments close 30 November on NIST’s draft rewrite of its OT security guide, which adds water, food, rail, maritime and building-automation coverage
item.category: Guidance — NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 4 draft (released 21 Sep 2026); public comments close 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST’s draft Revision 4 of SP 800-82, the US government’s main guide to operational technology security, is open for public comment until 30 November 2026. The draft reorganises the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with risk management now led by the Govern function, and adds sector material for building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels, and industrial IoT connected to cloud services. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and detection, protecting system-management functions, and applying zero-trust principles. Many regulators, insurers and auditors use 800-82 as a reference, so its final wording can shape what operators are asked to show; the comment window is the chance for practitioners to flag guidance that would not work on a plant floor. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft (21 Sep 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Sep 2026) - Forward-looking: public comments close 30 Nov 2026
